question.text: Which of the following best describes the purpose of 'portable alpha' or alpha-beta separation?

answer.text: Deliver market returns at zero cost
Separate alpha generation from market exposure, letting each be managed independently

explanation.text: The Logic: Portable alpha = decouple alpha source (e.g., long-short equity) from beta exposure (e.g., S&P 500 futures overlay), sizing each independently. The Trap: Not zero-cost; not max tracking error; doesn't eliminate risk — just lets you pick which risks to take. Cross-Exam Context: X-A Investment Adviser mentions it; XXI-B integrates at PM-level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Portable alpha works for institutions with cheap beta-overlay financing — retail PMS typically can't access the leverage needed for the beta leg.
